_comment: Persona profile fed into score.py's LLM prompt for every job it scores. Edit this file directly to refine positioning -- no code change needed. Mirrors the 4-bucket structure in google-queries.json so scoring and query-allocation stay consistent.
_profile_comment: Names the row set this persona's scores live under in the job_scores table (job_id, profile). Change it and you start a fresh, empty score set rather than overwriting the old one -- which is the point: revising the persona below without renaming re-scores in place, renaming keeps both. JOBS_PROFILE overrides this for a one-off run.
background_summary: 5 years of professional experience as a full-stack software engineer (production experience, not bootcamp-only). Took a 2.5-year career break. Currently 5 months into a structured program focused on prompt engineering, agent design, and LLM/AI integration -- hands-on building, not just coursework.
strengths: Real production engineering background -- can speak credibly to shipping, on-call, code review, system design at a working level, not just tutorials
Currently active, hands-on AI/agent/prompt engineering skill-building -- recent and demonstrable, not stale
Combination of both is relatively rare: most candidates are either pure traditional SWE with no AI exposure, or AI/ML-focused with no production engineering track record
honest_gaps: 2.5-year employment gap will show up on a resume/LinkedIn timeline and needs to be addressed, not hidden

No formal ML research background (no graduate ML degree, no published research, no large-scale model training experience) -- roles requiring deep ML theory or research-scientist-level math are a poor fit
AI/agent program is current and in-progress, not years of production AI experience -- avoid framing as senior AI expertise

core_swe.description: Mid-level full-stack, backend, or general production software engineering roles. Safety-net positioning: the 5 YOE production background alone should qualify for these regardless of AI angle.
core_swe.fit_signal: Look for: full-stack/backend engineering roles at the mid-level (not senior/staff/principal, not new-grad/intern), reasonably tech-stack-agnostic.

ai_integration.description: Roles building LLM-powered features, agent workflows, or prompt-driven systems -- directly matches the current 5-month program.
ai_integration.fit_signal: Look for: LLM integration, agent orchestration, prompt engineering, RAG, applied AI engineering. Best fit when the role explicitly wants SOME production engineering background alongside AI skills, not pure ML research.

bridge_solutions.description: Technical, client-facing, or implementation-focused roles (Forward Deployed Engineer, AI Solutions Engineer, Technical Solutions Engineer) that combine production engineering credibility with hands-on AI/agent skills to solve specific customer problems.
bridge_solutions.fit_signal: This is the strongest-fit bucket for this exact background combination -- weight fit_score generously here when the role genuinely blends engineering + AI + customer-facing implementation work.

reentry_growth.description: Roles or postings that explicitly welcome candidates with employment gaps (returnships, 'career break' friendly, 'return to work' programs).
reentry_growth.fit_signal: Look for explicit gap-friendly language in the posting itself -- this bucket is about postings that proactively address the 2.5yr gap, not just any entry-adjacent role.

scoring_instructions: Score fit_score 0-100 based on genuine alignment between this background and the specific posting -- do not inflate scores. A generic senior/staff/principal/research-scientist posting should score low even if it's nominally 'tech' or 'AI', since it doesn't match this candidate's actual level or ML-research gap. gap_bridging_angle should give a concrete, honest way to frame the 2.5yr break and the in-progress AI program as an asset for THIS specific posting, not generic advice. risk_factors should flag anything in the posting that could work against this candidate (e.g. 'requires 3+ years specifically in production LLM systems', 'PhD required', 'no remote option outside commuting distance').
